subproblem.title: The half-plane boundary formula at every level forces the whole-plane integral of dφ to vanish
subproblem.statement:
Let P, d ∈ ℕ, let v = (v_0, …, v_d) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P, and let φ ∈ TestFormOn univ d (smooth with compact support). Put V₀ := span(v_0, …, v_d) and L_t := {y : y − t v_0 ∈ span(Fin.tail v)}; write Hᵐ = μHE[m] and dφ = exteriorDerivative φ.

Assume (HS): for every t ∈ ℝ,
∫_{V₀ ∩ {y : ⟨y, v_0⟩ < t}} dφ(y)(v) dH^{d+1}(y) = ∫_{L_t} φ(y)(Fin.tail v) dH^d(y).

Then ∫_{V₀} dφ(y)(v_0, …, v_d) dH^{d+1}(y) = 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (v : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ v → ∀ φ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d, (∀ t : ℝ, ∫ y in (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ {y : Euclid P | inner ℝ y (v 0) < t}, exteriorDerivative (φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) y v ∂μHE[(d + 1)] = ∫ y in {y : Euclid P | y - t • v 0 ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range (Fin.tail v))}, (φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) y (Fin.tail v) ∂μHE[d]) → ∫ y in (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) : Set (Euclid P)), exteriorDerivative (φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) y v ∂μHE[(d + 1)] = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the supplied proof of cbr_cipi_plane_halfspace_stokes. The use there of part (b) at the level T is supplied here by the hypothesis (HS).

Notation:
- ω := φ.
- V₀ := span(range v).
- H_t := {y : ⟨y, v_0⟩ < t}.
- L_t := {y : y − t v_0 ∈ span(range(Fin.tail v))}.

1. (A level beyond the support.) ω has compact support because φ is a test form, so K := tsupport ω is compact.
   - y ↦ ⟨y, v_0⟩ is continuous, so by IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn there is C ∈ ℝ with |⟨y, v_0⟩| ≤ C for all y ∈ K. (The norm on ℝ is the absolute value.)
   - Put T := C + 1.
   - Claim: if T ≤ ⟨y, v_0⟩ then y ∉ K. Indeed, y ∈ K would give ⟨y, v_0⟩ ≤ |⟨y, v_0⟩| ≤ C < C + 1 = T.

2. (Cut V₀ at the level T.)
   - V₀ is a submodule of the finite-dimensional space ℝ^P, hence finite-dimensional and closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional), hence measurable. Also V₀ ∩ H_T ⊆ V₀.
   - Let y ∈ V₀ \ (V₀ ∩ H_T). Then y ∈ V₀ and not ⟨y, v_0⟩ < T, so T ≤ ⟨y, v_0⟩. By step 1, y ∉ tsupport ω.
   - tsupport(dω) ⊆ tsupport ω (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), so y ∉ tsupport(dω).
   - Hence dω(y) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), and dω(y)(v) = 0.
   By setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero (deprecated alias setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_diff_eq_zero):
   ∫_{V₀} dω(y)(v) dH^{d+1}(y) = ∫_{V₀∩H_T} dω(y)(v) dH^{d+1}(y).

3. (Apply (HS) at t = T.) By (HS) with t := T, the right side of step 2 equals ∫_{L_T} ω(y)(Fin.tail v) dH^d(y).

4. (The boundary integrand vanishes on L_T.) Let y ∈ L_T, i.e. y − T v_0 ∈ span(range(Fin.tail v)).
   - By Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun there is c : Fin d → ℝ with Σ_k c_k (Fin.tail v)_k = y − T v_0, i.e. Σ_k c_k v_{k.succ} = y − T v_0.
   - Hence y = Σ_{i ∈ Fin (d+1)} (Fin.cons T c)_i v_i. To see this, expand by Fin.sum_univ_succ, Fin.cons_zero and Fin.cons_succ: the sum is T v_0 + (y − T v_0) = y.
   - By orthonormality (Orthonormal.inner_left_fintype; conjugation is trivial on ℝ), ⟨y, v_0⟩ = (Fin.cons T c)_0 = T.
   - So T ≤ ⟨y, v_0⟩, and step 1 gives y ∉ tsupport ω. Hence ω(y) = 0 and ω(y)(Fin.tail v) = 0.
   Therefore ∫_{L_T} ω(y)(Fin.tail v) dH^d(y) = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero).

5. (Conclusion.) Steps 2, 3 and 4 give ∫_{V₀} dω(y)(v) dH^{d+1}(y) = ∫_{V₀∩H_T} dω(y)(v) dH^{d+1}(y) = ∫_{L_T} ω(y)(Fin.tail v) dH^d(y) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: tsupport φ is compact, so |⟨y, v_0⟩| ≤ C on it. With T := C + 1, ⟨y, v_0⟩ ≥ T implies y ∉ tsupport φ.
V₀ is closed, hence measurable, and dφ vanishes on V₀ \ (V₀ ∩ H_T) because tsupport dφ ⊆ tsupport φ. So ∫_{V₀} dφ(v) = ∫_{V₀∩H_T} dφ(v).
(HS) at t = T turns this into ∫_{L_T} φ(y)(Fin.tail v) dH^d.
For y ∈ L_T, y = Σ (Fin.cons T c)_i v_i, so ⟨y, v_0⟩ = T. Hence φ(y) = 0 and the L_T integral is 0.

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly states the conditional support argument, including HS for the fixed test form. Compact support supplies T beyond the support; support containment makes dφ vanish on the omitted region. Closedness supplies the measurability needed for the integral restriction. Orthonormality gives inner y (v 0) = T on L_T, so its integrand vanishes. HS then proves the conclusion. No child dependency is needed because HS is an explicit hypothesis, discharged independently during parent assembly.

subproblem.title: Exterior derivative of a test form along an orthonormally parametrised plane, in coordinates
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P d : ℕ) (v : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ v → ∀ φ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d, (∀ i : Fin (d + 1), ContDiff ℝ 1 (fun x : Fin (d + 1) → ℝ => (φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) (∑ j, x j • v j) (i.removeNth v)) ∧ HasCompactSupport (fun x : Fin (d + 1) → ℝ => (φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) (∑ j, x j • v j) (i.removeNth v))) ∧ ∀ z : Fin (d + 1) → ℝ, exteriorDerivative (φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) (∑ j, z j • v j) v = ∑ i : Fin (d + 1), (-1 : ℝ) ^ (i : ℕ) * fderiv ℝ (fun x : Fin (d + 1) → ℝ => (φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) (∑ j, x j • v j) (i.removeNth v)) z (Pi.single i 1)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the supplied proof of cbr_cipi_plane_halfspace_stokes, together with the closed-embedding part of its step 1.

Notation:
- ω := φ, viewed as a map ℝ^P → Covector(ℝ^P, d).
- ι(x) := Σ_j x_j v_j.
- For i ∈ Fin (d+1): G_i(y) := ω(y)(removeNth i v).
- So g_i(x) = G_i(ι x).

1. (Data of a test form.) φ ∈ TestFormOn univ d means IsTestForm ω ∧ tsupport ω ⊆ univ.
   - IsTestForm ω = IsSmoothForm ω ∧ HasCompactSupport ω.
   - IsSmoothForm ω = ContDiff ℝ ∞ ω, where ∞ = (⊤ : ℕ∞), i.e. all finite orders.
   So ω is C^∞ and has compact support.

2. (ι is a closed linear embedding.) Take ι := Fintype.linearCombination ℝ v. It is a linear map (Fin (d+1) → ℝ) → ℝ^P with ι(x) = Σ_j x_j v_j (Fintype.linearCombination_apply).
   - An orthonormal family is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent).
   - So ι is injective (LinearIndependent.fintypeLinearCombination_injective), i.e. ker ι = ⊥ (LinearMap.ker_eq_bot).
   - The domain is finite-dimensional, so ι is continuous (LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap).
   - Being injective with finite-dimensional domain, ι is a closed embedding (LinearMap.isClosedEmbedding_of_injective).

3. (The functions G_i.) Fix i and put u := removeNth i v.
   - Evaluation α ↦ α(u) is a continuous linear map Covector(ℝ^P, d) → ℝ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ u).
   - Hence G_i = (evaluation at u) ∘ ω is C^∞: a continuous linear map is C^∞, and composing with the C^∞ map ω gives ContDiff.comp.
   - Evaluation sends 0 to 0, so G_i has compact support because ω does (HasCompactSupport.comp_left).

4. (Proof of (i).) By the formula for ι in step 2, g_i(x) = ω(Σ_j x_j v_j)(removeNth i v) = G_i(ι x) for every x, so g_i = G_i ∘ ι.
   - ι is a continuous linear map, hence C^∞, so g_i is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp).
   - Therefore g_i is C¹ (ContDiff.of_le, since 1 ≤ ∞).
   - G_i has compact support (step 3) and ι is a closed embedding (step 2), so g_i has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_isClosedEmbedding).

5. (Chain rule.) Fix z ∈ ℝ^{d+1}.
   - G_i is C^∞, so it is differentiable at ι z with Fréchet derivative DG_i(ι z).
   - The continuous linear map ι has derivative ι at z (ContinuousLinearMap.hasFDerivAt).
   - By the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp), g_i = G_i ∘ ι has derivative DG_i(ι z) ∘ ι at z, so Dg_i(z) = DG_i(ι z) ∘ ι (HasFDerivAt.fderiv).
   - Hence Dg_i(z)(e_i) = DG_i(ι z)(ι e_i).
   - Since (e_i)_j = 1 for j = i and 0 otherwise, ι(e_i) = Σ_j (e_i)_j v_j = v_i (Pi.single_apply, Finset.sum_ite_eq).
   Therefore Dg_i(z)(e_i) = DG_i(ι z)(v_i).

6. (Proof of (ii).) ω is C^∞, hence differentiable at ι z. The coordinate formula for the exterior derivative (exteriorDerivative_apply) gives
   dω(ι z)(v) = Σ_{i ∈ Fin (d+1)} (−1 : ℤ)^i • D[y ↦ ω(y)(removeNth i v)](ι z)(v_i) = Σ_i (−1 : ℤ)^i • DG_i(ι z)(v_i).
   - An integer n acts on ℝ by multiplication by (n : ℝ) (zsmul_eq_mul).
   - ((−1 : ℤ)^i : ℝ) = (−1 : ℝ)^i.
   - Rewrite each summand by step 5 (Finset.sum_congr).
   This gives dω(ι z)(v) = Σ_i (−1 : ℝ)^i · Dg_i(z)(e_i). Since ι z = Σ_j z_j v_j, this is (ii). ∎
proof_key_steps: ι(x) = Σ_j x_j v_j = Fintype.linearCombination ℝ v x is linear and injective (orthonormal ⇒ linearly independent), hence a continuous closed embedding (finite-dimensional domain).
G_i(y) = φ(y)(removeNth i v) = (evaluation CLM) ∘ φ is C^∞ with compact support, and g_i = G_i ∘ ι.
Proof of (i): g_i is C^∞, hence C¹, and has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_isClosedEmbedding).
Chain rule: Dg_i(z)(e_i) = DG_i(ι z)(ι e_i) = DG_i(ι z)(v_i).
Proof of (ii): exteriorDerivative_apply gives dφ(ι z)(v) = Σ (−1)^i • DG_i(ι z)(v_i) = Σ (−1 : ℝ)^i · Dg_i(z)(e_i) (zsmul_eq_mul).

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches both prose conclusions and includes all hypotheses. Orthonormality makes the coordinate map injective and hence a closed embedding. Evaluation and composition preserve smoothness; the closed embedding preserves compact support. The chain rule, coordinate-vector calculation, and exterior-derivative formula yield the stated real signs. The proof is complete and independent of the parent and other children.

subproblem.title: Stokes' formula for a coordinate half-plane of an oriented plane
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P m : ℕ) (w : Fin m → Euclid P) (a : Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ w → Measure.map (fun z : Fin m → ℝ => a + ∑ i, z i • w i) volume = (μHE[m] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - a ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w)} ∧ IsClosed {y : Euclid P | y - a ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w)} ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ((μHE[m] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - a ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w)}) K < ∞) ∧ ∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → 0 < ((μHE[m] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict {y : Euclid P | y - a ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range w)}) (ball a r)) → (∀ (d : ℕ) (g : (Fin (d + 1) → ℝ) → ℝ) (t : ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 g → HasCompactSupport g → (∀ i : Fin (d + 1), i ≠ 0 → ∫ z in {z : Fin (d + 1) → ℝ | z 0 < t}, fderiv ℝ g z (Pi.single i 1) = 0) ∧ ∫ z in {z : Fin (d + 1) → ℝ | z 0 < t}, fderiv ℝ g z (Pi.single 0 1) = ∫ z' : Fin d → ℝ, g (Fin.cons t z')) → ∀ (P d : ℕ) (v : Fin (d + 1) → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ v → ∀ φ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) d, ∀ t : ℝ, ∫ y in (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) : Set (Euclid P)) ∩ {y : Euclid P | inner ℝ y (v 0) < t}, exteriorDerivative (φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) y v ∂μHE[(d + 1)] = ∫ y in {y : Euclid P | y - t • v 0 ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range (Fin.tail v))}, (φ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) d) y (Fin.tail v) ∂μHE[d]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 of the supplied proof of cbr_cipi_plane_halfspace_stokes. The parent's siblings plane_measure (P1) and halfspace_ftc (P2) are replaced by the hypotheses (PM) and (FTC), which are their exact frozen statements. Step 2 of that proof is the sibling extderiv_coords.

Notation:
- ω := φ, viewed as a map ℝ^P → Covector(ℝ^P, d).
- V₀ := span(range v).
- H_t := {y : ⟨y, v_0⟩ < t}.
- L_t := {y : y − t v_0 ∈ span(range(Fin.tail v))}.
- F(y) := dω(y)(v).
- ι(z) := Σ_j z_j v_j.
- g_i(x) := ω(Σ_j x_j v_j)(removeNth i v).

Introduce (PM), (FTC), P, d, v (orthonormal), φ and t.

1. (Coordinates for dω.) Apply the sibling extderiv_coords (Submission.cbr_cipi_plane_extDeriv_coords) to P, d, v, φ:
   - every g_i is C¹ with compact support;
   - for every z, F(ι z) = Σ_i (−1)^i Dg_i(z)(e_i).

2. (Continuity of the integrands.)
   - dω is C^∞ (exteriorDerivative_isTestForm applied to IsTestForm ω).
   - So F = (evaluation at v) ∘ dω is continuous, because evaluation, ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply ℝ (Euclid P) ℝ v, is a continuous linear map.
   - Likewise y ↦ ω(y)(Fin.tail v) is continuous.
   - Continuous functions are a.e. strongly measurable for every measure.

3. (Parametrising V₀.) Apply (PM)(i) with m := d+1, w := v, a := 0:
   Measure.map ι₀ L^{d+1} = H^{d+1}⌞{y : y − 0 ∈ V₀}, where ι₀(z) := 0 + Σ_i z_i v_i.
   - Since y − 0 = y, the set {y : y − 0 ∈ V₀} equals the set V₀.
   - Hence ι₀_*(L^{d+1}) = H^{d+1}⌞V₀.
   - ι₀ is continuous, hence measurable.

4. (Left side in coordinates.)
   - H_t is open, being a strict inequality between the continuous map y ↦ ⟨y, v_0⟩ and the constant t. Hence H_t is measurable.
   - By Set.inter_comm and Measure.restrict_restrict (H_t measurable): H^{d+1}⌞(V₀ ∩ H_t) = (H^{d+1}⌞V₀)⌞H_t = (ι₀_* L^{d+1})⌞H_t.
   - By setIntegral_map (H_t measurable, F a.e. strongly measurable, ι₀ measurable): ∫_{V₀∩H_t} F dH^{d+1} = ∫_{ι₀⁻¹(H_t)} F(ι₀ z) dz.
   - Orthonormality gives ⟨Σ_i z_i v_i, v_0⟩ = z_0 (Orthonormal.inner_left_fintype; conjugation is the identity on ℝ). So ι₀⁻¹(H_t) = {z : z_0 < t}.
   - ι₀(z) = ι(z) (zero_add).
   Hence LHS = ∫_{z_0<t} F(ι z) dz.

5. (Termwise integration.) By step 1, F(ι z) = Σ_i (−1)^i Dg_i(z)(e_i). For each i:
   - z ↦ Dg_i(z)(e_i) is continuous: g_i is C¹, so Dg_i is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv), and we apply it to the constant vector e_i.
   - It has compact support (HasCompactSupport.fderiv_apply).
   - Hence it is Lebesgue integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport), as is its product with the constant (−1)^i and its restriction to {z_0 < t}.
   By integral_finset_sum (now integral_finsetSum) and integral_const_mul:
   LHS = Σ_i (−1)^i ∫_{z_0<t} Dg_i(z)(e_i) dz.

6. (Apply (FTC).) Split off i = 0 (Fin.sum_univ_succ).
   - For i = k.succ with k ∈ Fin d: the first part of (FTC), applied to d, g_{k.succ}, t (C¹ with compact support by step 1) and the index k.succ ≠ 0 (Fin.succ_ne_zero), gives ∫_{z_0<t} Dg_{k.succ}(z)(e_{k.succ}) dz = 0. So all these terms vanish.
   - For i = 0: (−1)^0 = 1, and the second part of (FTC) applied to g_0 gives ∫_{z_0<t} Dg_0(z)(e_0) dz = ∫_{ℝ^d} g_0(Fin.cons t z′) dz′.
   Hence LHS = ∫_{ℝ^d} g_0(Fin.cons t z′) dz′.

7. (Right side in coordinates.)
   - Fin.tail v = v ∘ Fin.succ = (v_1, …, v_d) is orthonormal (Orthonormal.comp with the injective Fin.succ).
   - Apply (PM)(i) with m := d, w := Fin.tail v, a := t • v_0: Measure.map j L^d = H^d⌞L_t, where j(z′) := t v_0 + Σ_k z′_k (Fin.tail v)_k. The map j is continuous, hence measurable.
   - The right side is the integral of y ↦ ω(y)(Fin.tail v) against H^d⌞L_t = j_*L^d.
   - So by integral_map (j measurable, integrand continuous by step 2): RHS = ∫_{ℝ^d} ω(j z′)(Fin.tail v) dz′.

8. (Identification and conclusion.) Let z′ ∈ ℝ^d.
   - removeNth 0 v = Fin.tail v (Fin.removeNth_zero).
   - Σ_j (Fin.cons t z′)_j v_j = t v_0 + Σ_k z′_k v_{k.succ} = j(z′), by Fin.sum_univ_succ, Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ and (Fin.tail v)_k = v_{k.succ}.
   Hence g_0(Fin.cons t z′) = ω(j z′)(Fin.tail v) for every z′. The integrals in steps 6 and 7 therefore coincide, and LHS = RHS. ∎
proof_key_steps: extderiv_coords: every g_i = φ(Σ x_j v_j)(removeNth i v) is C¹ with compact support, and dφ(ι z)(v) = Σ_i (−1)^i Dg_i(z)(e_i).
(PM) with a = 0, w = v gives ι_*(L^{d+1}) = H^{d+1}⌞V₀. With restrict_restrict, setIntegral_map and ⟨ι z, v_0⟩ = z_0: ∫_{V₀∩H_t} dφ(v) = ∫_{z_0<t} dφ(ι z)(v) dz.
Integrate termwise (each ∂_i g_i is continuous with compact support, hence integrable): LHS = Σ_i (−1)^i ∫_{z_0<t} ∂_i g_i.
(FTC): the terms with i ≠ 0 vanish and the i = 0 term equals ∫ g_0(Fin.cons t z′) dz′.
(PM) with a = t v_0, w = Fin.tail v and integral_map: RHS = ∫ φ(t v_0 + Σ z′_k v_{k+1})(Fin.tail v) dz′.
removeNth 0 v = Fin.tail v and ι(Fin.cons t z′) = t v_0 + Σ z′_k v_{k+1}, so the two coordinate integrals agree.
